tb21_profile.skill: Design queries to a black-box numeric function and solve for its hidden internals: locate ReLU kinks by finite differencing, recover each hidden neuron's hyperplane normal, and assemble A1 up to permutation and scaling despite floating-point noise
tb21_profile.domain: Neural networks (one-hidden-layer ReLU nets), numerical linear algebra and floating-point analysis, Python/NumPy, ML-security model extraction
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec of a published extraction algorithm via black-box probing; graded by matrix equivalence up to permutation and scale

TMax-15K.reason: Reverse-engineer a hidden 5x3 projection matrix behind a ReLU by querying an oracle with basis vectors - the same linear-layer-plus-ReLU weight recovery TB2.1 asks for.
Design synthetic inputs, query a stripped scorer and fit regression to recover its coefficients exactly - query design plus numerical parameter recovery.
Compute gradients of an objective by central finite differences with a prescribed step h; step-size and cancellation control is the crux of probing a ReLU net.
Treat a stripped binary as a black box, craft small inputs to deduce the exact function it computes, then reimplement it equivalently.
Generate dummy data to probe an oracle, observe input-output behaviour and identify the transform (quantile/CDF mapping) it implements.
Script a parameter sweep over a black-box binary to deduce its formula; systematic querying rather than static reverse engineering.
Exactly TB2.1's object: a 10-input MLP with a ReLU hidden layer, weights in numpy, vectors in .npy files - but the weights are given, not recovered.
Take an oracle's labels for chosen inputs and solve a least-squares system for the underlying linear weights - the solve step of an extraction attack.
Implement power iteration to recover the dominant eigenvector of a covariance matrix; recovering directions that are only defined up to scale.
Run an MLP with a ReLU hidden layer by hand from extracted weights; builds the forward-pass algebra an extraction attack must invert.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Use symbolic execution to solve for the input a binary accepts; recovering a hidden value a black box never reveals directly.
Symbolically explore an authentication binary and partition final states by output - mapping the full behaviour of an opaque function.
Explore all paths with angr and classify which inputs reach which outcome; systematic query design over an unknown function.
Recover a crackme's password by analysis and explicitly not by brute force - the same 'reason about the internals, do not search blindly' discipline.
Three separate binaries each hiding a different secret; repeated black-box-to-secret recovery with verification by running the binary.
Train SVR models and produce numeric estimates through a scientific pipeline; same numeric-ML ecosystem, no extraction.
Train and run a scikit-learn classifier end to end; touches the model layer TB2.1 attacks but exercises no probing.
Train an embedding model and compute a numeric shift between corpora; fit-a-model-and-report-a-number, no hidden-parameter recovery.
Load a .npy array with numpy/pandas, clean it and write the result; only the array-IO surface of TB2.1 overlaps.
Read /app/input.npy, drop NaN rows and print the shape - the same file format and nothing else.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Recover a hidden magic constant by solving the constraints a binary imposes via dynamic symbolic execution - inferring internals no output reveals.
Symbolically execute a crackme to find the accepting input; solving for unknowns of an opaque function rather than guessing.
Analyse all terminal states of a binary under angr to discover the backdoor; enumerating an unknown function's behaviour systematically.
Explore every execution path of a binary symbolically - the query-coverage mindset needed to find every ReLU's activation boundary.
Probe where float arithmetic loses resolution by computing 2**e + 1 - 2**e; precisely the precision budget that decides a usable finite-difference step.
Demonstrate catastrophic cancellation that IEEE floats cannot handle, on random 100x100 matrices; the exact numerical hazard in differencing a net.
Recover a plaintext by symbolic execution over the transformation that produced the ciphertext; inverting an opaque function.
Fixed-point/float conversions with exact bit budgets; representation and rounding awareness, but no model and no probing.
Define an nn.Linear-based network and profile its parameter statistics; the same PyTorch layer algebra, purely descriptive.
Split data, train a linear-kernel model and evaluate it; a linear decision function, but fitted from data rather than extracted.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Fix least-squares residuals for a 2D right-hand side to match numpy; lstsq over many probe points is how the recovered weights are solved for.
The flop handler for matrix-multiply ops is broken; requires reasoning about the matmul shapes inside a traced network.
Weight-init fan_in/fan_out mode and the relu nonlinearity gain were swapped; genuine reasoning about a linear layer's weight statistics.
Recompute precise batch-norm statistics over many forward passes; accumulating an accurate estimate from repeated network evaluations.
Analysis of a tiny nn.Linear + ReLU network; the same architecture TB2.1 attacks, but inspected rather than extracted.
Model-statistics formatting for an nn.Linear(10,10)+ReLU net - the exact input width of TB2.1, but the work is string formatting.
smooth_l1_loss branches wrongly around its knot; a piecewise-linear function whose breakpoint must be handled exactly, like a ReLU kink.
Rounding of fractional float indices is wrong; small floating-point handling bug in an array library.
Tensor-to-numpy shape handling is broken; the torch/numpy boundary the extraction script lives on, but nothing numerical.
dmatrix builds design matrices from a formula; constructing the matrix a linear system is solved against, one step removed.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: An eigenvector permutation-invariance test fails on a different CPU; comparing quantities defined only up to permutation and sign under FP noise, exactly TB2.1's grading.
A forward simulation's derivative (rhoDeriv, getJ, Jvec) becomes inconsistent after dpred; reasoning about a model's Jacobian versus its forward evaluations.
Return the R factor from Gram-Schmidt so an SVD can be assembled; recovering the factorisation hidden behind an orthogonalisation routine.
eig returns the wrong structure for a 1x1 matrix; eigendecomposition edge cases in an arbitrary-precision numeric library.
lu_solve fails on batched inputs; solving many small linear systems at once is how per-neuron equations get resolved.
Add a transposed option to linalg.solve so gradients avoid an extra transpose; linear-solve APIs and their derivatives.
A converter must reproduce a fitted discriminant model's parameters and output shapes in another runtime - transplanting learned weights faithfully.
Batch-mode posterior covariance indexing is wrong; careful shape and linear-algebra bookkeeping over stacked models.
A saved model's rescaling layer does not round-trip on reload; reconstructing a network's exact layer parameters from a serialized form.
Eigenvector dimensions break after a refactor; eigen-decomposition plumbing, same numerical-library territory.

final_top10.reason: Recover a hidden linear layer's matrix behind a ReLU by querying an oracle with basis vectors, then reproduce its output exactly - the same attack, smaller.
Design synthetic queries against a stripped binary and fit them to recover its exact coefficients; query design plus numerical parameter recovery.
Estimate gradients of an objective by central finite differences at a prescribed step - the probe TB2.1 uses to find each ReLU's kink.
Craft inputs for a stripped binary to deduce the exact function it computes and reimplement it equivalently - pure black-box inference.
Recover a hidden constant by solving the constraints a binary imposes through dynamic symbolic execution rather than by guessing.
Generate probe data, observe an oracle's input-output pairs and identify the transformation it applies before reimplementing it.
Eigenvector permutation invariance fails under floating-point differences - comparing objects defined only up to permutation and sign, as TB2.1 grades A1.
Script a systematic parameter sweep over a black box to deduce its formula instead of reading its disassembly.
Solve symbolically for the input a binary accepts; recovering unknowns of an opaque function by constraint solving.
A 10-input MLP with a ReLU hidden layer, numpy weights and .npy vectors - TB2.1's exact object, with the weights handed over instead of stolen.

notes: There is no model-extraction or cryptanalytic-weight-recovery task anywhere in the pool, so nothing scores 5 except task_001030_45a9959c, which is genuinely close: query an oracle implementing linear-then-ReLU with basis vectors and recover the hidden matrix. Beyond that the pool splits into two disjoint families that each cover half the skill, and I ranked accordingly: (a) black-box probing / secret recovery - TMax's oracle-reimplementation tasks, TerminalWorld's and Recursive-Task-Synthesis's angr and crackme tasks, which teach 'design queries, solve for the hidden thing, never brute force'; and (b) the numerical side - finite differences, catastrophic cancellation, least squares, eigenvectors-up-to-permutation - which lives in TMax's numerics tasks, tw_92921/tw_125169, and SWE-Rebench's pytensor/pymor/mpmath/pyg items. The many TMax 'reconstruct this MLP from the given weights and run inference' tasks are a domain bullseye (one of them, task_003103_c5ee5fa5, even uses a 10-input net with a ReLU hidden layer and .npy files) but a skill miss, because the weights are handed over; I kept two of them at ranks 7 and 10 of TMax and did not inflate them. Recursive-Task-Synthesis's shortlist was almost entirely the ~169 duplicated 'drop NaN rows from /app/input.npy' chores, retrieved purely on the .npy token - I discounted those to overall 2 and went to its crackme/angr family instead. SWE-Smith has no numerical-attack material; its fvcore tasks are the right stack (nn.Linear, ReLU, matmul flop counting) with little transferable skill, so it tops out at 3.
